blindSummary: Same-sex conduct is criminalised as acts "contrary to morality or against nature" under a 2020 penal code (up to 2 years), and the law is actively enforced: two women were detained in June 2024 after asking a religious dignitary to marry them, and convicted in December 2024 (released after serving time). There is no legal gender recognition; a small, socially conservative island nation.
blindOutOfScope: The 2024 prosecution relates to same-sex conduct (climate); it shows active enforcement.

The same foreign government's 2010 human-rights report on this country: general human-rights baseline (poor prisons, restrictions on movement/press/religion, discrimination against women) with limited LGBT-specific content.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (March 2026): a penal-code article punishes 'any act of a sexual nature that is contrary to public decency or against nature' with 6 months to 2 years and fines; no SOGI protections, no legal gender recognition, no intersex protections; in 2022 a leaked video allegedly led to the first imprisonment for same-sex intimacy; in June 2024 two women were arrested after asking a religious dignitary to marry them (convicted December 2024, sentenced to time served); the government repeatedly refuses UN decriminalisation recommendations.
An LGBT-focused news site (Dec 2024): a court in this country convicts a female same-sex couple and sentences them to months in jail.
blindTangential: The 2020 criminalisation and the 2024 prosecution show active enforcement of morality provisions — trans visitors are captured via birth-sex status; the case also signals risk for anyone in a same-sex relationship.
